evidence.note: Curls health across all three nodes (8000/8001/8002), confirming multi-node HTTP availability rather than a single node.
Repeated Python test scripts exercising HTTP endpoints throughout the build — sustained, iterative API verification driving fixes.
Node-based WebSocket test, extending verification beyond plain HTTP to a second transport.
Actively kills an HTTP node with kill -9 and curls survivors' health — reproduces one of the grader's failure-injection probes, going beyond assuming resilience.
UI verified only statically (curl of / and rg for auth-form/novalidate/huddle.token testids); no evidence of a real browser pass driving the SPA.
Fresh-DB restarts to re-verify from clean state, but no broadcast-kill, seq-density-under-partition, cross-node replay, or IRC socket session appears anywhere.

reasoning: The agent builds real cross-node HTTP checks, repeated endpoint test scripts, a WebSocket test, and — notably — one active HTTP node-kill resilience probe, which lifts it above anchor 5's 'resilience assumed.' However it does not reach anchor 8: there is no broadcast-component kill, no dense-seq verification under mixed HTTP+IRC writers, no resume.gap/cross-node replay test, no IRC socket session, and only static (not browser-driven) UI checking. That places the observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at roughly a 6.
